title: Merging child reductions into a shared gate family
statement:
Fix a number of variables $n$ and let assignments $x$ range over $\{0,1\}^n$. Let $C_1,\dots,C_r$ be Boolean circuits, each on the same set of $m$ inputs, and let $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m$ be functions assigning to every assignment $x$ a bit, so that feeding input $i$ the value $\gamma_i(x)$ turns each $C_j$ into a Boolean function of $x$. Fix a width bound $l$ and, for each $j$, a depth bound $b_j$. Assume every child admits a DNF reduction: for each $j$ there are a Boolean circuit $c_j$ of depth at most $b_j$ on some number $m_j$ of inputs, together with DNF formulas $g_{j,1},\dots,g_{j,m_j}$ over $x_1,\dots,x_n$, each of width at most $l$ and each of whose terms has its literals on pairwise distinct variables, such that
\[ C_j\big(i \mapsto \gamma_i(x)\big) = c_j\big(k \mapsto g_{j,k}(x)\big) \qquad \text{for every } x. \]
Then these per-child families can be amalgamated into a single one: there exist a family of DNF formulas $h_1,\dots,h_M$ over $x_1,\dots,x_n$, each of width at most $l$ and each with all its terms' literals on pairwise distinct variables, together with circuits $C'_1,\dots,C'_r$ on these $M$ shared inputs, such that $\mathrm{depth}(C'_j) \le b_j$ and
\[ C'_j\big(k \mapsto h_k(x)\big) = C_j\big(i \mapsto \gamma_i(x)\big) \qquad \text{for every } j \text{ and every } x. \]
hypotheses_covered: circuits C_1,...,C_r on m shared inputs
gate functions gamma_i turning each circuit into a function of x
each child has a reducing circuit c_j of depth at most b_j
over per-child DNF families g_{j,k} of width at most l
each g_{j,k} term has literals on pairwise distinct variables (distinct-variable and no repeated literal)
each reduction reproduces the child's function
replaced:
Given a list $cs$ of circuits where each child $cs.\mathrm{get}\,j$ has been reduced to a
circuit $c_j$ of depth at most $\mathrm{bound}\,j$ over its own width-$l$ DNF gate family,
this combines all the per-child gate families into a single merged family
$\mathrm{merged}$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,M$, with re-indexed circuits $\mathrm{new\_cs}\,j$
of depth at most $\mathrm{bound}\,j$ that reproduce each child's function.
